items.stem: What best describes a 'golden path' in platform engineering?

options.text: A supported, opinionated default route for a common task that is the easiest way to do it well
options.rationale: Correct: golden paths make the good way the easy way while allowing exceptions.

options.text: The only permitted way to do anything, with no exceptions ever
options.rationale: Golden paths are defaults with escape hatches, not rigid mandates.

options.text: A premium paid tier of the platform
options.rationale: It is a supported default route, not a pricing tier.

options.text: A manual approval queue for all changes
options.rationale: That is a ticket process, the opposite of a paved road.

items.explanation: Correct: golden paths make the good way the easy way while allowing exceptions.
items.domain_ref: Internal developer platforms and golden paths

items.stem: Which two characteristics distinguish genuine self-service from a disguised ticket queue? (Select TWO)

options.text: A developer can provision what they need on demand without waiting for a human
options.rationale: Correct: on-demand provisioning is the essence of self-service.

options.text: The capability is exposed through an API or portal that automates the request
options.rationale: Correct: automation behind the request removes the human bottleneck.

options.text: Every request is routed to an operator to action manually
options.rationale: Manual actioning is a ticket queue, not self-service.

options.text: Requests are fulfilled only during a weekly change window
options.rationale: Waiting for a window is not on-demand self-service.

items.explanation: Correct: on-demand provisioning is the essence of self-service.; Correct: automation behind the request removes the human bottleneck.

items.stem: Why is treating the platform 'as a product' important for its success?

options.text: Because adoption is voluntary, so the platform must meet real developer needs to be used
options.rationale: Correct: product thinking keeps the platform useful enough that teams choose it.

options.text: Because it lets the platform team ignore user feedback
options.rationale: Product thinking centres on user feedback, not ignoring it.

options.text: Because it guarantees every team must use it by law
options.rationale: Mandates are not product thinking and often backfire.
Products require ongoing maintenance and iteration.

items.explanation: Correct: product thinking keeps the platform useful enough that teams choose it.
